scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Soo-ah Kim and I'm 75. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello, Ms. Kim. I’m sorry to hear about the confusion regarding your billing while you were away, and I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with your subscription?
Of course. My account number is 8829-4410 and the email is sooah.kim@email.com.
Thank you for that information. For security, could you please confirm your billing zip code and the last four digits of the payment method on file?
The zip code is 90210 and the card ends in 4492.

Perfect, thank you for verifying those details. I have located your account and the charge in question. While our standard 'Service Satisfaction Policy' dictates that refund requests must be submitted within 30 days of the renewal date, I can see that your account has been in good standing for several years. Given your circumstances, I am authorized to make a one-time exception to this policy.
Oh, that is such a relief to hear! Thank you so much for understanding.

You are very welcome, Ms. Kim. I have processed the refund of $49.99 back to your original payment method. You should see the credit appear in your account within 3 to 5 business days, depending on your financial institution. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: The agent verified the customer's identity and account, acknowledged the policy limit, and utilized discretionary authority to grant a one-time exception for a refund due to the customer's long-standing account history.
